title: Messi in Tears After Argentina's Three-Goal Comeback Stuns Egypt in 13 Frantic Minutes
excerpt: Trailing 2-0 with 11 minutes left, the defending champions score three — Romero, Messi, Fernandez in stoppage time — to survive the round of 16 and reach the World Cup quarterfinals
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Argentina staged a stunning comeback, scoring three goals in 13 minutes to win 3-2 against Egypt.
  • Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament, reclaiming the Golden Boot lead.
  • Argentina will face Switzerland in the World Cup quarterfinals after this dramatic victory.
  • Egypt led 2-0 until the 79th minute, showcasing a remarkable performance before the collapse.
  • Messi expressed deep emotion, highlighting the team's resilience in a knockout match.
For 79 minutes in Atlanta, Egypt were writing one of the greatest upsets in World Cup history. Then Lionel Messi reminded the world why he is the greatest player to ever live. Argentina came from 2-0 down to beat Egypt 3-2 in one of the most dramatic comebacks in World Cup history, scoring three goals in 13 extraordinary minutes to book their quarterfinal spot. Messi, 39, was in floods of tears at the final whistle — and everyone understood why. ## Egypt's Dream, Argentina's Nightmare Egypt came into the round of 16 as heavy underdogs but played with a fearlessness that had Argentina reeling. Yasser Ibrahim opened the scoring, and Mostafa Zico doubled the lead. Messi had already squandered an early penalty in the 21st minute, his effort saved by goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir, and Argentina looked rudderless. At 2-0 down with 11 minutes remaining, Argentina's World Cup defence appeared to be ending not with a whimper but with an embarrassment. The 68,000 fans inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium sensed history — and for the Egyptian contingent, it was the right kind. ## The 13-Minute Blitz > **""They turned around a 2-0 deficit in a World Cup knockout match."** Then came the comeback that will be replayed for decades. In the 79th minute, Messi swung in a cross from the right and Cristian Romero rose unmarked to power a header past Shobeir. Argentina had a pulse. Four minutes later, it was the captain himself. After substitute Lautaro Martinez and Gonzalo Montiel kept the ball alive near the Egyptian goal, Messi lashed a shot into the net to make it 2-2. His eighth goal of the tournament put him back atop the Golden Boot standings — one clear of Kylian Mbappe and Erling Haaland. Egypt were on loose legs now, the composure that had carried them for 80 minutes evaporating in real time. In the second minute of stoppage time, Enzo Fernandez met Lisandro Martinez's cross with a thumping header across goal and into the far corner. 3-2. Atlanta erupted. ![Lionel Messi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/27/Lionel_Messi_NE_Revolution_Inter_Miami_7.9.25-178.jpg) ## Messi's Last Dance Continues "Honestly, what the group did today was crazy," Messi said after the match, still visibly emotional. "They turned around a 2-0 deficit in a World Cup knockout match. This group has showed once again that it competes, it never gives up."
Argentina's Dramatic Comeback
79th Minute
Cristian Romero scores, making it 2-1.
83rd Minute
Lionel Messi equalizes with a powerful shot, 2-2.
90+2 Minute
Enzo Fernandez scores the winning goal, 3-2.
Manager Lionel Scaloni could barely speak in his post-match interview, managing only: "What a group of players, brother," before walking away. The victory means Argentina advance to face Switzerland in the quarterfinals on Sunday in Kansas City. One day after his eternal rival Cristiano Ronaldo bowed out with Portugal's elimination, Messi's last World Cup dance continues. ## The Quarterfinal Picture With the round of 16 now complete, the World Cup's final eight is set: - **France vs Morocco** — Thursday, July 9 in Foxborough - **Spain vs Belgium** — Friday, July 10 in Los Angeles - **Norway vs England** — Saturday, July 11 in Miami - **Argentina vs Switzerland** — Sunday, July 12 in Kansas City

The Spain-Belgium clash in LA and Norway-England in Miami will draw massive crowds, while Argentina's meeting with Switzerland in Kansas City pits the defending champions against a team on their best World Cup run since 1954. *Sources: Reuters, The Wall Street Journal, Sporting News, NBC Sports, USA Today*
